rationale: Repair all boards to use only own formatter entries, with a safe direct-loop alternative prepared before baseline execution. Target O(n*m + L) with offset row/column counts and pre-trim padded output units, excluding formatter work. Unsupported authored dimensions remain visible as the goal but the uncertain estimate is hidden under issue419, preserving25 XP.

objective: Append a fresh todo with a calculated ID that cannot be overwritten by wider draft data.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Appending immutable application records is practical state work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Compile-time views versus runtime fields and assignment order transfer to other adapters.

relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Spreading a wider draft after the calculated ID lets its existing ID replace the chosen one.

defects: Copy and hints overstated Omit as preventing all runtime extra IDs.
Reference/senior spread draft after id, so a compatible wider variable could override it.
Junior rebuilt only declared fields and lost shallow metadata.
The original id-first reference passed all old fresh-draft examples.
rationale: Clarify Omit as a compile-time view with excess-property checking for fresh literals, not runtime sanitization. Place calculated id last in all boards/scaffold/steps and use spread in junior. Define dense frozen-capable lists through1000, positive bounded integer IDs with duplicates allowed, exact old Todo references, own draft metadata including Symbol/literal __proto__, independent plain mutable appended records and unchanged sources. Three runtime assertions inspect an own wider draft ID999 versus calculated8, opaque metadata/prototype safety,1000 repeated high/low IDs and100 extra draft fields with fresh empty-list outputs. Add a static compatible wider-ID variable round trip with readonly input and mutable Todo[] output, preserving the old fresh-literal ID rejection. Target linear todo count plus copied field count. No real ID allocator, profile or database sequence changes.

objective: Model exactly five weekday literals with Exclude and a boolean predicate that narrows both branches correctly.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Exclude and type predicates remain current TypeScript fundamentals.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Finite literal-domain filtering is practical type-safe application logic.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Runtime truth and honest true/false-branch narrowing transfer to other guards.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The seven-literal teaching domain fits a foundational utility-type exercise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: An overly narrow predicate alias can pass runtime checks while making valid weekday values unassignable.

defects: Existing runtime coverage already exercised all seven days, but static checks omitted Tuesday/Thursday membership.
A Weekday alias incorrectly excluding Tuesday still passed every old runtime and type assertion.
Exact boolean, fixed-domain and repeatability rules were implicit.
rationale: Retain all correct boards and accept a modern inferred-predicate alternative on the actual TypeScript5.9.3 checker. State the exact primitive lowercase Day domain, all five weekday members and no holiday/locale schedule promise. One runtime assertion checks all seven exact booleans repeatedly without input changes. One static assertion assigns all five weekday literals and verifies both predicate branches; it catches the deliberately over-narrow alias although its runtime values all pass. Preserve existing Saturday/Sunday rejection checks. Target constant work because the domain and weekend set are fixed. Do not claim the already exhaustive runtime domain as a newly discovered gap.
